description: Agent-based mobile-money simulator calibrated against one month of aggregated, anonymized real transaction logs from a mobile money service operating in an African country. Kaggle-hosted as "Synthetic Financial Datasets For Fraud Detection" (scaled to 1/4 of the original simulation size).
source: Lopez-Rojas, E.A., Elmir, A., Axelsson, S. "PaySim: A financial mobile money simulator for fraud detection." 28th European Modeling and Simulation Symposium (EMSS), Larnaca, Cyprus, 2016.
applicability_notes: `type` (CASH_IN, CASH_OUT, DEBIT, PAYMENT, TRANSFER) is the closest thing to a merchant-category field; it is a transaction-type taxonomy, not an MCC, so it is used here only as a coarse categorical-cardinality reference (5 categories), not mapped onto our MCC codes.

`step` buckets transactions into simulated hours (1 step = 1 hour, 744 steps = 31x24h), so PaySim IS usable for a coarse hour-of-day proxy (step mod 24) even though it publishes no direct hour-of-day histogram -- treat any such histogram as a derived quantity, not a directly cited one.
No published network/graph-degree summary exists, even though `nameOrig`/`nameDest` exist per row (computing a real degree distribution would require the raw file, which is not downloaded here).

Fraud in this dataset is restricted by construction to TRANSFER and CASH_OUT types only -- a well-documented data-generating-process quirk, not something to expect in our generated data (our fraud rows are labelled independently).

balance_drain_fraud_mechanism.value: PaySim's fraud generation is explicitly designed around account takeover → TRANSFER → CASH_OUT sequences (documented in the PaySim paper), where receiver accounts are rapidly liquidated after receiving funds. This mechanism is the signature of balance-drain-exit fraud.
balance_drain_fraud_mechanism.source: Lopez-Rojas et al., PaySim paper: fraud generation process description; Kaggle dataset card notes on isFraud generation logic restricted to TRANSFER and CASH_OUT types.

n_steps.source: Kaggle dataset card; PaySim paper describes step as one simulated hour.

fraud_count.source: Kaggle dataset card / widely repeated in EDA write-ups; 8,213 of 6,362,620 rows have isFraud=1 (~0.129%).

fraud_rate.source: Derived from the two published counts above (8213 / 6362620), not itself a directly quoted percentage.

is_flagged_fraud_threshold.unit: currency units (simulator's own unit, not INR/USD-pegged)
is_flagged_fraud_threshold.source: PaySim paper and dataset card: isFlaggedFraud fires on any single transfer attempt exceeding 200,000, an illustrative hard-coded business rule, not a real-world regulatory limit.

fraud_restricted_to_types.source: Dataset card and near-universally confirmed in public EDA of this dataset: PAYMENT/CASH_IN/DEBIT rows never have isFraud=1.

type_distribution_approx.source: Rounded from figures commonly reported across multiple independent public EDA notebooks of this exact dataset. The original paper/dataset card does not publish an exact type-mix table, so treat the precise percentages as approximate; the reliable part is the ordering (CASH_OUT and PAYMENT dominate and are roughly comparable in share, CASH_IN is a distant third, TRANSFER and DEBIT are minority types).

amount_shape.value: heavily right-skewed, multiple orders of magnitude range; amounts are simulated from clustered behavior fitted to the source mobile-money logs rather than a single parametric family
amount_shape.source: PaySim paper section on amount generation (cluster-based sampling from real log statistics); exact parametric form not reproduced here.

usable_for_validation_areas: categorical_cardinality (transaction `type`, 5 categories -- coarse proxy, not MCC)
temporal_patterns (hour-of-day only, via step mod 24; no day-of-week signal since 744 steps do not align to a stated calendar week)
amount_distribution (overall shape only, scale-invariant comparison -- simulator's currency unit is not INR-pegged)
not_usable_for: transactions_per_party (nameOrig/nameDest exist per-row but per-party aggregate counts are not published, and we do not download the raw file)
